name: Tadalafil once daily for ED
question: Does once-daily tadalafil improve erectile function compared with placebo in men with erectile dysfunction?

design.population: 268 men aged at least 18 years, in monogamous relationships with female partners, with erectile dysfunction for at least three months; prior ineffective sildenafil treatment and prior tadalafil trial participation were excluded.
design.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 352–353; Table 1, p 354

verdictNote: Both tadalafil doses improved all three primary erectile-function measures versus placebo.
takeaway: In men with erectile dysfunction, tadalafil 5 mg or 10 mg once daily improved IIEF erectile-function scores and diary-reported penetration and intercourse completion versus placebo over 12 weeks.

reports.label: Placebo-controlled trial
reports.citation: Porst H, Giuliano F, Glina S, et al. "Evaluation of the Efficacy and Safety of Once-a-Day Dosing of Tadalafil 5mg and 10mg in the Treatment of Erectile Dysfunction: Results of a Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial." *Eur Urol.* 2006;50(2):351-359. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2006.02.052

results.measure: Mean IIEF erectile-function domain change from baseline to endpoint (points)
results.note: Randomized arm sizes: 109 (5 mg), 105 (10 mg), 54 (placebo). Endpoint mean scores were 22.8, 22.8 and 15.0, respectively. Primary efficacy analysis included patients with baseline and at least one post-baseline measurement, using last observation carried forward for missing IIEF-EF scores; 14 men with baseline scores 26–30 remained in the prespecified analysis. Dunnett-adjusted pairwise P values are reported; confidence intervals were not reported.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical analysis, p 353; Results, Table 2, p 355

results.note: Per-patient mean percentage of successful-penetration attempts; randomized arm sizes were 109, 105 and 54. Endpoint means were 79.4%, 81.2% and 51.7%, respectively. Efficacy analysis required baseline and at least one post-baseline measurement; Dunnett-adjusted pairwise P values are reported without confidence intervals.
results.locator: Full text, Outcome measures and Statistical analysis, pp 352–353; Results, Table 2, p 355

results.note: Per-patient mean percentage of successful-intercourse attempts; randomized arm sizes were 109, 105 and 54. Endpoint means were 67.2%, 72.8% and 36.7%, respectively. Efficacy analysis required baseline and at least one post-baseline measurement; Dunnett-adjusted pairwise P values are reported without confidence intervals.
results.locator: Full text, Outcome measures and Statistical analysis, pp 352–353; Results, Table 2, p 355

results.measure: Patients reporting improved erections at endpoint
results.note: Global Assessment Question among respondents; arm-specific respondent counts were not reported.
results.locator: Full text, Outcome measures and Statistical analysis, pp 352–353; Secondary efficacy endpoints, p 354

results.measure: IIEF-EF score 26–30 at endpoint among men with baseline IIEF-EF score below 26
results.note: The 14 men with baseline IIEF-EF scores 26–30 were excluded from this secondary endpoint; arm-specific eligible counts and responder counts were not reported.
results.locator: Full text, Outcome measures, p 352; Secondary efficacy endpoints, p 354; Table 1, p 354

values.t10: Dyspepsia 12/105 (11.4%); headache 11/105 (10.5%); back pain 10/105 (9.5%); upper abdominal pain 9/105 (8.6%); myalgia 7/105 (6.7%)

harms.label: Death and myocardial infarction
harms.locator: Full text, Safety, p 355; Fig. 1, p 353
harms.note: One participant in the 5-mg group died with renal cell carcinoma; the investigator judged the death unrelated to study drug. No myocardial infarctions occurred.

delivery.label: Daily treatment
delivery.value: Placebo, tadalafil 5 mg or tadalafil 10 mg once daily in a nominal 12-week study; treatment lasted 12–15 weeks and randomization was 1:2:2. Participants were instructed to take one dose around the same time each day.

delivery.label: Adherence and completion
delivery.value: Compliance, defined as taking at least 70% of doses between visits, was 94.2% with 5 mg, 93.0% with 10 mg and 96.2% with placebo. Tadalafil recipients averaged 6.5 doses per week and placebo recipients 6.6; 234/268 (87.3%) completed the study.
delivery.locator: Full text, Patients, p 354; Safety, p 355

reports.label: Open-label extensions
reports.citation: Porst H, Rajfer J, Casabé A, et al. "Long-Term Safety and Efficacy of Tadalafil 5 mg Dosed Once Daily in Men with Erectile Dysfunction." *J Sex Med.* 2008;5(9):2160-2169. doi:10.1111/j.1743-6109.2008.00935.x
reports.followUp: One-year extension of the Porst trial; separate two-year extension of another daily-tadalafil trial
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Study Populations and Study Designs, pp 2161–2162; Figure 1, p 2162

results.measure: Mean IIEF erectile-function domain change from baseline before any study drug to one year (points)
results.note: In the one-year open-label cohort, mean IIEF-EF score rose from 13.7 before any study drug (229 evaluable) to 24.1 at one year (213 evaluable), then fell to 16.0 after four treatment-free weeks (206 evaluable). Efficacy analyses required baseline and at least one extension observation; the one- and two-year cohorts came from different parent trials. No prespecified significance threshold or comparator was reported.
results.locator: Full text, Efficacy Measures, p 2163; Efficacy and Figure 3, pp 2164–2166; Table 4, p 2167

results.endpoint: Normal erectile function at one year and after cessation
results.measure: IIEF-EF score at least 26 among evaluable men with baseline score below 26; persistence four weeks after cessation among those normal at one year who entered follow-up

values.t5: 117/202 (57.9%) at one year; 28/114 (24.6%) after four treatment-free weeks

results.note: The 114 follow-up entrants were a subset of the 117 men with normal function at one year. Both denominators are completer/evaluable subsets, not all 234 extension entrants.

delivery.label: One-year extension completion
delivery.value: The one-year open-label tadalafil 5-mg extension enrolled 183 completers of the randomized trial and 51 newly enrolled men because 51 French completers could not continue under local regulations. In total, 208/234 (88.9%) completed the extension and 207 completed the four-week treatment-free period.
delivery.locator: Full text, Study Populations and Study Designs, pp 2161–2162; Figure 2A, p 2164

delivery.label: One-year extension adherence
delivery.value: 215/226 (95.1%) with complete dosing information took at least 70% of daily doses between visits; cumulative tadalafil exposure was 225.1 patient-years.

reports.label: Response after cessation
reports.citation: Porst H, Glina S, Ralph D, Zeigler H, Wong DG, Woodward B. "Durability of Response Following Cessation of Tadalafil Taken Once Daily as Treatment for Erectile Dysfunction." *J Sex Med.* 2010;7(10):3487-3494. doi:10.1111/j.1743-6109.2010.01908.x
reports.followUp: One year of open-label tadalafil 5 mg, followed by four treatment-free weeks
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Study Procedures and Figure 1, pp 3488–3489

results.measure: Maintained improvement in ED severity category or normal function four weeks after stopping tadalafil
results.note: Among 158 men with scores at baseline, after one year, and four weeks after cessation, 136 improved at least one ED severity category or maintained normal function during treatment. Of those 136, 73 (53.7%) had returned to their baseline or a worse category after cessation. This retrospective analysis made no statistical comparisons or prespecified success test.
results.locator: Full text, Main Outcome Measures and Statistical Methods, p 3489; Results, pp 3490–3491

results.measure: Improved at least one ED severity category or maintained normal IIEF-EF function from baseline to end of extension
results.locator: Full text, Improvements in Erectile Function, p 3490

results.endpoint: ED severity category after four treatment-free weeks
results.measure: Category disposition among the 136 men improved or normal at end of one-year treatment

values.t5: Durable 63/136 (46.3%): 38/63 (60.3%) kept the end-of-treatment category and 25/63 (39.7%) declined but remained above baseline; no durability 73/136 (53.7%): 50/73 (68.5%) returned to baseline category and 23/73 (31.5%) worsened

results.locator: Full text, Durability of Response and Figure 2, pp 3490–3491

delivery.label: Post-treatment analysis set
delivery.value: After the randomized 12-week phase and one-year tadalafil 5-mg open-label extension, 160 original-trial participants completed four treatment-free weeks; 158 had IIEF-EF scores at all three required time points and entered the retrospective analysis. The 51 newly enrolled extension patients lacked the original randomized baseline and were excluded.
delivery.locator: Full text, Study Procedures and Statistical Methods, pp 3488–3489; Results, p 3490
